'''Ibrahim Khalil''' ({{langx|ar|إبراهيم خليل}}; 1957 &ndash; 22 or 24 December 2011) was a Sudanese insurgent leader who was the founder of the [[Justice and Equality Movement]] (JEM) which he led until his death. In the 1990s Ibrahim served in several state governments of Sudan.

==Early life==
Ibrahim was born in Sudan in 1957.<ref name=independent>{{cite news |first=Eric |last=Law |title=Dr Khalil Ibrahim: Leader of the Darfur rebels in Sudan |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/dr-khalil-ibrahim-leader-of-the-darfur-rebels-in-sudan-6281848.html |work=[[The Independent]] |date=27 December 2011 |access-date=2012-01-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107012909/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/dr-khalil-ibrahim-leader-of-the-darfur-rebels-in-sudan-6281848.html |archive-date=7 November 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> Ibrahim was from the Koba branch of the [[Zaghawa people|Zaghawa]] ethnic group,<ref name=independent/> which is located mainly in [[Sudan]], with a minority on the Chad side of the border. He was an enthusiastic supporter of the [[National Islamic Front]] (NIF) [[1989 Sudanese coup d'état|seizure of power]] under the direction of [[Islamism|Islamist]] [[Hassan al-Turabi]] in 1989.<ref name=independent/>

==Political career==
{{More citations needed section|date=January 2024}}
Ibrahim served as the state minister for education in Darfur between 1991 and 1994 in [[al-Fashir]], [[North Darfur]]. A physician, Ibrahim spent four months in 1992 to fight [[Sudan People's Armed Forces]]. By Ibrahim's own account, he was disaffected with the Islamist movement by 2000 after seeing the economic neglect of the NIF, as well as its support to armed militias. At this time, he became part of a [[covert cell]] of Islamists who were seeking to change the NIF from inside. Ibrahim went on to serve as the state minister for social affairs in [[Blue Nile, Sudan|Blue Nile]] in 1997 before a post as adviser to the governor of [[South Sudan|Southern Sudan]] in [[Juba]] in 1998. However, others noted that he never received a national level appointment. Ibrahim's colleague in JEM, Ahmad Tugod, stated, "Khalil is not a first or even second class political leader. [...] He struggled all of his life to get a post in [[Khartoum]]."<ref name="autogenerated1">Flint, Julie and [[Alex de Waal]], ''Darfur: A Short History of a Long War'', Zed Books, London March 2006; {{ISBN|1-84277-697-5}}, p. 91</ref>

He quit the post in August 1998, several months before the end of his appointment, and formed an NGO called "Fighting Poverty". In December 1999, when al-Bashir sidelined al-Turabi with the help of [[Ali Osman Taha]], Ibrahim was in the [[Netherlands]], studying for a master's degree in public health at [[Universiteit Maastricht]]. In the meantime, the structure of covert cells that Ibrahim had helped set up in 1994 had spread to Khartoum. The dissidents, dubbing themselves "The Seekers of Truth and Justice" published the ''[[The Black Book: Imbalance of Power and Wealth in the Sudan|Black Book]]'' in 2000, claiming Riverine Arabs {{clarify|date=January 2024}} dominated political power and resources.

In 2001, Ibrahim was one of twenty people sent out of the country by the dissidents to go public. In August 2001, Ibrahim published a press release from the [[Netherlands]], in which he announced the formation of the [[Justice and Equality Movement]]. The JEM has a relatively small ethnic base of support, limited to the Kobe Zaghawa, including many kinsmen from across the Chadian border.<ref>Al-Jazeera English YouTube, [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TZzywqPJ7IE ''Sudan opposition arm group fights to forge a new reformed and just country for all Sudanese on the basis of citizenship'', 15 April 2009] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160415094954/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TZzywqPJ7IE |date=15 April 2016 }}</ref>

==Darfur conflict==
On 5 March 2002, Ibrahim claimed credit for initiating a government revolt. This apparent claim of the landmark attack on [[Golo, Sudan|Golo]], actually carried out by the [[Sudan Liberation Movement|Sudan Liberation Army]] (SLA), was mocked by the SLA and the JEM was forced to back away from their announcement. Regardless, the JEM and the anti-government SLA formed a loose alliance in prosecuting the [[Darfur conflict]].{{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}

In May 2006, the JEM rejected the [[Abuja Accord (Sudan)|Abuja peace process]], which was accepted by the faction of the SLA led by [[Minni Minnawi]], but rejected by the smaller SLA factions. On 30 June 2006, Ibrahim, [[Khamis Abdalla]], the leader of an SLM faction, [[Sharif Harir]] and [[Ahmed Ibrahim (Sudanese politician)|Ahmed Ibrahim]], co-leaders of the [[National Democratic Alliance (Sudan)]], founded the [[National Redemption Front]] rebel group in [[Asmara]], [[Eritrea]] but which is based in [[Chad]].

Ibrahim lived in exile in [[Libya]] from May 2010 to September 2011, when the [[2011 Libyan civil war|Libyan civil war]] compelled him to flee across the [[Sahara]] and return to [[Darfur]]. The [[Sudan]]ese government and diplomatic sources accused Ibrahim's group of rebels in Libya of fighting as mercenaries for Libyan strongman [[Muammar Gaddafi]] during the war, charges to which Ibrahim never responded, neither being proved.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sudantribune.com/article39631/|agency=Sudan Tribune|date=11 September 2011|access-date=24 August 2025|title=EXCLUSIVE: JEM Leader says he has arrived in Darfur}}{{dead link|date=November 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-14881745|publisher=BBC News|date=12 September 2011|access-date=3 October 2011|title=Darfur rebel leader Khalil Ibrahim flees Libya|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110918145659/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-14881745|archive-date=18 September 2011|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Death==
Ibrahim died either on 22 December 2011 after an air strike by the Sudanese armed forces<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-16328441|publisher=BBC News|date=25 December 2011|access-date=25 December 2011|title=Sudan Darfur rebel Khalil Ibrahim 'killed by army'|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111225062626/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-16328441|archive-date=25 December 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> or on 24 December 2011, two days after being injured in fighting in [[North Kordofan]], west of [[Wad Banda]].<ref name=independent/>
